concepts.title: Open workbench
concepts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: high fidelity concept screenshot for FIRELINE, an accessible open-ended engineering game about Ontario wildfire modelling and quantum feature selection.
Style: exquisite retro industrial pixel-art game interface with precise large readable forms, deep petrol teal painted metal, dark green CRT glass, amber phosphor, mint traces, copper wiring, restrained screws and seams. Mature cohesive art direction, physical controls with delightful affordances. Crisp intentional pixel texture, subtle volumetric glow, not blurry AI noise. Orthographic straight-on full-screen widescreen 16:9 composition, screen fills image edge to edge, no surrounding computer or room.
Design constraints: most of the frame is the playable machine or map, tiny integrated control chrome; no large header/footer, no card dashboard, no paragraphs, no steps 1–6, no badges, no unnecessary branding or caution banners, no characters, no watermark. Show an actual player decision with visible consequences. Only use the exact short labels explicitly given below, otherwise icons, diagrams and sparse numeric markings. Any numerical game readouts are illustrative concept values, not claimed research results. Make the layout immediately understandable and professionally implementable as a browser game.
Primary request: hero gameplay concept of a single unified workbench. A full Ontario raster map including the southern peninsula and Toronto/GTA occupies the upper left, with rich forest pixels, dark water and sparse amber reported-fire dots. The center is a large magnetic assembly surface with a player-built four-input machine: draggable slim climate/forest sensor tiles wired through small encoder modules into a luminous kernel mesh and one output gauge. One unused sensor tile is visibly being dragged into a free socket with a mint ghost placement and a precise copper cable following it. The right edge holds a small beautiful wireframe quantum sphere and a tiny comparison trace. A low integrated tool tray at the bottom has several distinct parts and a substantial RUN lever. The assembled machine, not UI explanation, is the star. Ontario map and wires have proper legible silhouettes, no sprawling arbitrary noodles.
Text verbatim: "FIRELINE" in a small engraved corner, "TEMP", "RAIN", "FOREST", "LAG", "RUN".
